failures.name: Mars 96
failures.cause: The Blok D-2 upper stage did not complete its second burn to leave Earth orbit, and the craft reentered; the inquiry could not tell whether the stage or the spacecraft's control system was at fault.

failures.name: Navstar GPS SVN 42
failures.cause: The case of GEM strap-on number 2 cracked and burst seconds after liftoff; the board found the motor had been damaged by a support in a new transport system.

failures.name: Tselina-2 No. 13L
failures.cause: The first stage engine failed at about T+48 s after a pitch deviation; no detailed root cause was published.

failures.name: Progress M-34 / Mir collision
failures.cause: In a manual (TORU) docking test without range data, the cosmonaut misjudged the closing speed; Progress hit Mir's Spektr module and holed it.

failures.name: Iridium MS-2
failures.cause: GCAT records that a fairing thermal blanket was damaged and harmed one Iridium satellite; no investigation detail was found.

failures.name: IRS-1D
failures.cause: A pressure (helium) leak in the fourth stage cut its performance and left IRS-1D in a low orbit.

failures.name: TEAMSAT
failures.cause: Swirl in the Vulcain engine flow made an unexpected roll torque; the roll control used up its capacity and the core stage shut down early, leaving a low orbit.

failures.name: SCD-2A
failures.cause: One of the four first stage strap-on motors failed to ignite, the rocket went off course and was destroyed by range safety.

failures.name: Asiasat 3
failures.cause: A defective wear coating on seals in the Blok DM high-pressure LOX pump cut oxygen flow at the second burn start and the engine auto-shut down after about 1 s.

failures.name: EROS A
failures.cause: The rocket failed during the second stage burn and fell into the Mediterranean; no root cause was published.

failures.name: COMETS
failures.cause: A brazing defect in the LE-5A second stage combustion chamber cooling tubes let hot gas leak and the second burn ended early.

failures.name: SOHO
failures.cause: At the L1 halo orbit, errors in modified gyro command procedures during routine operations left a gyro off, and the craft lost attitude and contact for about three months. It was recovered, though later gyro losses followed.

failures.name: MERCURY 3
failures.cause: Damaged (chafed) wiring shorted and caused power transients to the guidance computer, which lost attitude reference and the vehicle broke up.

failures.name: Galaxy X
failures.cause: The control system was not designed for a roll oscillation mode; the solid motor TVC hydraulic fluid ran out and the vehicle lost control.

failures.name: Paektusan 1 flight
failures.cause: The third stage failed; North Korea claimed success and no root cause was published.

failures.name: Globalstar Z1
failures.cause: A flight control computer fault shut down the second stage engine at T+272 s; detailed findings were not published.

failures.name: NEAR Shoemaker
failures.cause: The first rendezvous burn at Eros aborted when a lateral acceleration limit in the software was exceeded, and flawed fault-response software then fired thrusters thousands of times and wasted fuel. Arrival slipped by over a year; the board also cited weak testing and procedures.

failures.name: DSP 19?
failures.cause: Thermal tape wrapped around an electrical connector kept it from separating, so the IUS stages did not separate and the satellite was left in a useless orbit.

failures.name: Ikonos 1
failures.cause: The fairing did not separate; reports say the shock of the circumferential ordnance disconnected the cable to the longitudinal ordnance.

failures.name: Milstar DFS-3
failures.cause: A roll rate filter constant was entered into the Centaur software as -0.1992476 instead of -1.992476, causing loss of roll control and RCS depletion.

failures.name: Orion 3
failures.cause: The RL10B-2 combustion chamber ruptured because of a poor braze joint, and the second burn failed.

failures.name: Gran' No. 45
failures.cause: A stray aluminium particle and a welding defect started a fire in a second stage engine built during poor workmanship years at Voronezh.

failures.name: Mars Climate Orbiter
failures.cause: Ground software gave thruster impulse data in pound-force seconds instead of newton seconds, so navigation errors built up and the orbiter passed too low through the atmosphere and was destroyed.

failures.name: Ekspress-A No. R 001
failures.cause: Silica, metal and fabric particles left in a second stage engine gas generator and turbine during manufacture ignited the turbopump.

failures.name: MTSAT
failures.cause: An LE-7 fuel turbopump inducer blade broke from fatigue caused by cavitation, and the first stage engine stopped.

failures.name: Deep Space 2 Amundsen probe
failures.cause: The penetrator probe released from Mars Polar Lander was never heard from after impact; the review board listed possible causes (such as radio failure on impact or batteries) but could not find one.

failures.name: Deep Space 2 Scott probe
failures.cause: The second penetrator probe was also never heard from after impact; no cause was found.

failures.name: Mars Polar Lander
failures.cause: The review board's most probable cause: leg deployment jolts set touchdown sensor flags that the software did not clear, so the descent engines shut off about 40 m up and the lander fell.

failures.name: SACI-2
failures.cause: The second stage did not ignite; the investigation found flame penetration into the second stage block and its forward flexible heat shield.

failures.name: ASTRO E
failures.cause: The graphite nozzle throat insert of the first stage motor failed, so the vehicle lost control authority and the upper stages could not reach orbit.

failures.name: ICO F1
failures.cause: Ground software failed to send the command to close a valve in the second stage pneumatic system, helium was lost and steering failed.

failures.name: DM-F3
failures.cause: The second stage shut down early and left the demo payload in a lower orbit; no cause was published.

failures.name: QuickBird 1
failures.cause: The second stage failed to restart to circularize the orbit; oxidizer contamination was suggested but no official cause was found.

failures.name: Gonets-D1 No. 19/20/21
failures.cause: Telemetry showed the third stage engine steering mechanism stuck, the stage veered off course and the computer shut the engine down at T+367 s.

failures.name: GSAT-1
failures.cause: The Russian cryogenic upper stage underperformed; sources disagree between a fuel booster turbopump fault and a wrong mixture ratio.

failures.name: Artemis
failures.cause: A combustion instability at Aestus ignition, from hydraulic coupling between the feed system and chamber, cut thrust and the stage ran out of one propellant 80 s early.

failures.name: Warfighter-1
failures.cause: The second stage thrust vector control actuator did not move when the motor ignited, and the vehicle could not reach orbit.

failures.name: CONTOUR
failures.cause: The spacecraft broke apart during its solid rocket motor burn to leave Earth orbit. The board found the most likely cause was overheating of the craft by the motor plume, which had not been properly analyzed because the motor was buried inside the spacecraft.

failures.name: HTSTL-1
failures.cause: The KT-1 failed in second stage flight; no cause was published.

failures.name: Foton-M No. 1
failures.cause: Debris ingested into the hydrogen peroxide pump of a strap-on (Blok D) cut lubricant to the turbopump and the engine failed at about T+29 s.

failures.name: Astra 1K
failures.cause: Excess fuel at Blok DM second burn ignition destroyed the engine; the commission blamed stray particles clogging drain manifolds or a gas generator valve but found no single root cause.

failures.name: Hot Bird 7
failures.cause: The Vulcain 2 nozzle cooling tubes failed because flight thermal and mechanical loads were higher than the design allowed, and the rocket lost control.

failures.name: STS-107 Columbia
failures.cause: A piece of foam from the external tank struck the left wing leading edge during launch and broke the reinforced carbon-carbon panels. Hot gas entered the wing during entry and the orbiter broke up; the board also blamed NASA's acceptance of repeated foam strikes; all seven crew died.

failures.name: Soyuz TMA-1
failures.cause: A fault in the descent control system, reported as a guidance software or control panel problem, switched the capsule to a ballistic entry. It landed about 460 km short of the target and the crew waited hours to be found.

failures.name: VLS-1 flight
failures.cause: An electrical fault (possibly static discharge) ignited one strap-on motor on the pad, killing 21 people; the report also cited poor wiring, documentation and management.

failures.name: KT-1 Test Payload
failures.cause: KT-1 launch attempt that failed; no details or cause were published.

failures.name: IGS Optical-2
failures.cause: Hot gas from a local SRB-A nozzle erosion damaged the separation fuse, so the right booster did not separate and the vehicle was destroyed.

failures.name: Nozomi (Planet-B)
failures.cause: A stuck valve during the 1998 Earth swingby burn wasted propellant and forced a long new route, then a 2002 solar flare damaged power circuits and froze the hydrazine, so the craft could not enter Mars orbit and was abandoned.

failures.name: Beagle 2
failures.cause: The lander touched down, but 2015 orbital images show that not all of its solar panels opened, blocking the radio antenna; why the panels did not deploy is not known.

failures.name: 'Ofeq-6
failures.cause: The third stage failed (likely did not ignite after second stage burnout); the root cause was never published.

failures.name: Genesis
failures.cause: The accelerometer g-switches that should have started the parachute sequence were installed upside down because of a design drawing error that reviews and tests missed. No parachute opened and the capsule hit the Utah desert, though much of the solar wind sample was recovered.

failures.name: HLV-OLDSP
failures.cause: Cavitation in the LOX feed lines made the depletion sensors read empty, so the core engines shut down early.

failures.name: Okean-O1 No. 9
failures.cause: The third stage apogee burn was too short and left a low perigee; no cause was published.

failures.name: Huygens (Cassini-Huygens)
failures.cause: During the Titan descent the Cassini receiver for Huygens channel A was never switched on because the command was left out of the sequence, so the Doppler wind experiment and half the images were lost.

failures.name: DART (Demonstration of Autonomous Rendezvous Technology)
failures.cause: The navigation software kept resetting its estimate to a biased GPS velocity, used up the propellant early and, in the close approach, did not see that it was too close; DART hit the MUBLCOM satellite.

failures.name: MS-1?
failures.cause: Unconfirmed KT-1 launch attempt; no details were published.

failures.name: Molniya-3K No. 12L
failures.cause: A racing fuel regulator on the core stage caused early kerosene depletion; the pump oversped and broke up, staging failed and the third stage was dragged off course.

failures.name: TPS Solar Sail
failures.cause: A first stage turbopump failed and the engine shut down at T+83 s; engines had been built without a design upgrade meant to fix this.

failures.name: Hayabusa (reaction wheels)
failures.cause: Two of the three reaction wheels failed (one in July 2005, one in October 2005) near Itokawa, leaving attitude control to thrusters and complicating the touchdowns.

failures.name: Cryosat
failures.cause: A missing command in the Breeze-KM flight software left the second stage burning to depletion, so it did not separate.

failures.name: Hayabusa (MINERVA hopper)
failures.cause: The MINERVA mini-lander was released by ground command while Hayabusa was rising away from Itokawa, so it drifted off into space instead of settling on the surface.

failures.name: Hayabusa
failures.cause: During the touchdowns on Itokawa the sampling projectile was not fired because of a problem in the onboard sequence, so only tiny grains were collected. The probe also lost reaction wheels, had a chemical thruster leak and ion engine faults, so the capsule came back in June 2010, three years late, with about 1,500 grains.

failures.name: Hayabusa (thruster leak)
failures.cause: A chemical thruster fuel leak after the touchdowns upset attitude and contact was lost for about seven weeks, which pushed Earth return back by three years.

failures.name: Arabsat 4A
failures.cause: A foreign particle blocked the nozzle of a hydraulic pump in the Breeze-M oxidizer supply and the second burn stopped early.

failures.name: Falconsat 2
failures.cause: A corroded aluminium B-nut on the fuel pump inlet leaked kerosene, which caught fire and cut pneumatic control of the engine.

failures.name: Insat 4C
failures.cause: A propellant regulator failure in one L40 strap-on engine caused loss of its thrust and the vehicle lost control.

failures.name: Dnepr Rideshare 4
failures.cause: The hydraulic gimbal drive of first stage combustion chamber 4 failed, producing thrust vector errors and loss of trajectory.

failures.name: Mars Global Surveyor
failures.cause: In its extended mission, a software update written to a wrong memory address drove a solar array against its stop; the resulting safe mode pointed a battery at the Sun, it overheated and failed, per NASA's review board.

failures.name: NSS 8
failures.cause: A foreign object (metal debris) entered the first stage RD-171 LOX pump, which failed at liftoff and the rocket fell back on the platform.

failures.name: AFSS/LCT2
failures.cause: LOX slosh in the second stage coupled with the control system; the growing oscillation led to early engine shutdown.

failures.name: INTRUDER 8?
failures.cause: A leaking valve on the Centaur LH2 tank lost fuel during coast and the second Centaur burn shut down early.

failures.name: INSAT 4CR
failures.cause: A control malfunction (stuck actuator) on one L40 strap-on built a high roll rate and led to early strap-on shutdown and a low orbit.

failures.name: JCSAT 11
failures.cause: A pyrotechnic cable damaged during manufacture kept the first and second stages from separating.

failures.name: Soyuz TMA-10
failures.cause: A damaged cable between the crew control panel and the descent computer caused the capsule to switch to a ballistic entry. It landed about 340 km short of the target under high g loads.

failures.name: Americom 14
failures.cause: A Breeze-M gas duct between gas generator and turbine ruptured because its walls were thinner than specified, and the second burn stopped early.

failures.name: Soyuz TMA-11
failures.cause: A pyrotechnic bolt failed to fire, so the propulsion module stayed attached to the descent module at the start of entry. The capsule entered hatch first until the link burned through, then flew a ballistic entry and landed about 475 km off target.

failures.name: ORS Trailblazer
failures.cause: Residual thrust from the new regeneratively cooled Merlin 1C pushed the first stage into the second stage after separation.

failures.name: Safir flight
failures.cause: Iranian launch reported as failed in second stage flight; no cause was published.

failures.name: Orbiting Carbon Observat
failures.cause: The fairing failed to separate; NASA later traced this and the Glory failure to faulty aluminium extrusions in the frangible joint supplied with falsified test results.

failures.name: Unha-2 flight
failures.cause: The third stage failed; no cause was published.

failures.name: Meridian No. 12
failures.cause: An upper stage engine shut down early and left the satellite in a low orbit; no cause was published.

failures.name: STSat-2
failures.cause: One half of the fairing failed to separate and the extra mass kept the satellite from orbit; no detailed root cause was published.

failures.name: Chandrayaan-1
failures.cause: After overheating problems and the loss of its star sensors, contact was lost when a power supply (DC-DC converter) failed, ending the mission after about 10 of the planned 24 months.

failures.name: Palapa D
failures.cause: The gas generator of one third stage engine burned through, most likely from foreign matter or humidity ice in the LH2 injectors.

failures.name: Spirit (MER-A)
failures.cause: After years past its 90-day goal, the rover (already driving on a dead front wheel) got stuck in soft soil in 2009, could not tilt its panels for winter, and fell silent in March 2010; NASA ended the mission in 2011.

failures.name: GSAT-4
failures.cause: The fuel booster turbopump of the Indian cryogenic stage failed shortly after ignition and the stage lost thrust.

failures.name: Shin'en
failures.cause: This university microsatellite, launched with Akatsuki, was never successfully heard from after launch and its Venus flyby was lost. Date is the launch date; the cause is not known.

failures.name: STSat-2B
failures.cause: The rocket exploded at T+137 s; Korean and Russian investigators disagreed (flight termination system versus first stage) and no agreed cause was published.

failures.name: Uragan-M No. 739
failures.cause: An error in the fuelling formula overloaded the Blok DM-03 with oxidizer, making the rocket too heavy to reach orbit.

failures.name: Akatsuki
failures.cause: During Venus orbit insertion a check valve in the pressurization line stuck (salt deposits from propellant vapor reaction), the engine ran oxidizer-rich, the nozzle was damaged and the burn cut off early. The craft entered Venus orbit with its attitude thrusters in 2015, in a much higher orbit.

failures.name: GSAT-5 Prime
failures.cause: Connectors carrying control signals to the strap-ons were pulled apart early, control was lost and the vehicle broke up.

failures.name: Musson-2 No. 11
failures.cause: The Breeze-KM upper stage malfunctioned and left the satellite in a wrong orbit; no root cause was published.

failures.name: Glory
failures.cause: The fairing failed to separate; NASA later traced this to faulty aluminium extrusions in the frangible joint supplied with falsified test results.

failures.name: Ekspress AM-4
failures.cause: The time window programmed for the Breeze-M gyro platform to turn was too short, so the stage pointed wrong for its burn.

failures.name: shijian shi yihao 04 xin
failures.cause: The link between second stage vernier engine 3 and its servo mechanism failed, and the stage lost attitude control.

failures.name: Progress 7K-TGM No.412
failures.cause: A blockage (contamination) in the third stage RD-0110 gas generator fuel line cut thrust and the engine shut down early.

failures.name: Phobos-Grunt
failures.cause: The craft's own engine never fired to leave Earth orbit; the Russian inquiry blamed radiation upsets in non-space-qualified memory chips that rebooted both flight computers, and it reentered in January 2012.

failures.name: Yinghuo-1
failures.cause: The Chinese orbiter rode on Phobos-Grunt and was lost with it when Phobos-Grunt failed to leave Earth orbit; Yinghuo-1 itself did not fail.

failures.name: Meridian No. 15L?
failures.cause: The third stage RD-0124 engine failed (gas generator or combustion chamber burn-through) and shut down early.

failures.name: Unha-3 flight
failures.cause: The first stage failed about a minute into flight; no cause was published.

failures.name: Fajr
failures.cause: Unconfirmed Iranian launch failure; no details were published.

failures.name: Telkom-3
failures.cause: A Breeze-M pressurization line component for the auxiliary tank was not made to specification, and the third burn stopped early.

failures.name: Fajr
failures.cause: Unconfirmed Iranian launch failure; no details were published.

failures.name: Dragon C103
failures.cause: A Merlin first stage engine lost chamber pressure and shut down; ISS safety rules then barred the second stage restart, so the Orbcomm secondary was left low.

failures.name: Yamal 402
failures.cause: Unusually warm propellant and engine heat soak-back let oxidizer gas reach the Breeze-M turbopump, damaging a bearing that failed in the fourth burn.

failures.name: Intelsat IS-27
failures.cause: The power supply to the first stage hydraulic pump failed, so the engine could not be steered and the rocket was shut down.

failures.name: Glonass-M 48,49,50
failures.cause: Three yaw angular rate sensors were installed upside down, so the control system steered the rocket the wrong way after liftoff.

failures.name: CBERS 3
failures.cause: Foreign debris blocked the fuel intake of one of two third stage YF-40 engines, which shut down early.

failures.name: Chang'e 3 Yutu rover
failures.cause: About six weeks after landing the rover lost the ability to drive because of a control circuit problem in its mobility system; it kept sending data while stationary. The root cause was not published.

failures.name: Ekspress AM-4R
failures.cause: A bearing in the third stage steering (vernier) engine turbopump was destroyed by high temperature and the stage failed.

failures.name: GalileoSat 5-6
failures.cause: A hydrazine line on Fregat ran next to a cold helium line and froze, causing loss of attitude; a design review gap.

failures.name: STEREO-B
failures.cause: Contact was lost during a planned test of the command-loss timer before solar conjunction. A failed inertial measurement unit leading to a spin and drained battery is suspected; the twin STEREO-A carried on.

failures.name: Ekspress AM-6
failures.cause: The Breeze-M left the satellite in an off-target orbit; Russian authorities never published the cause.

failures.name: Cygnus Orb-3
failures.cause: The LOX turbopump of one refurbished AJ26 engine failed seconds after liftoff and the vehicle fell back near the pad.

failures.name: SpaceShipTwo VSS Enterprise (PF04)
failures.cause: Suborbital. The copilot unlocked the feather system early during powered flight near Mach 1, and aerodynamic loads then deployed it, breaking the vehicle apart. The NTSB faulted Scaled Composites for not guarding against this single human error; the copilot died.

failures.name: Philae (Rosetta)
failures.cause: The anchoring harpoons did not fire and the cold-gas hold-down thruster did not work, so the lander bounced twice and settled in shadow. Its batteries ran out after about 60 hours.

failures.name: PROCYON
failures.cause: The ion engine stopped working in March 2015 (an electrical fault in the thruster), so the Earth swing-by and asteroid flyby could not be reached. Loss date is approximate.

failures.name: Progress 7K-TGM No. 426
failures.cause: A frequency-dynamic coupling between the third stage and spacecraft at separation ruptured the stage tanks, a design issue for this configuration.

failures.name: Mexsat-1
failures.cause: Excessive rotor imbalance in the third stage vernier engine turbopump caused vibration that destroyed the stage.

failures.name: Dragon C109
failures.cause: A steel strut holding a helium COPV in the second stage LOX tank broke below its rating, the COPV rose and overpressurized the tank.

failures.name: Hiakasat
failures.cause: The rocket lost control during first stage flight; no detailed cause was published.

failures.name: Kanopus-ST/KYuA-1
failures.cause: Kanopus-ST did not separate from the Volga upper stage, reportedly due to a defective separation mechanism.

failures.name: Gaofen 10
failures.cause: A blockage in the fuel line shut down one of two third stage YF-40 engines early (single report).

failures.name: Amos 6
failures.cause: Liquid oxygen pooled in buckles of a helium COPV liner in the second stage and ignited by friction during fuelling before a static fire.

failures.name: Juno
failures.cause: Two helium check valves feeding the main engine opened slowly, so the period reduction burn was cancelled and Juno stayed in its 53-day orbit instead of a 14-day orbit.

failures.name: Schiaparelli EDM
failures.cause: The inertial measurement unit saturated for longer than expected under the parachute; the software computed a negative altitude, released the parachute early, fired thrusters only briefly and the lander hit at about 540 km/h. The inquiry also faulted modelling and verification.

failures.name: Progress 7K-TGM No. 434
failures.cause: The third stage RD-0110 oxidizer pump caught fire and broke up the LOX tank, most likely from foreign particles or an assembly error.

failures.name: Superview 1/2
failures.cause: Staging and second stage cutoff were delayed and the satellites reached a lower orbit; no cause was published.

failures.name: TRICOM-1
failures.cause: Vibration rubbed a cable against the structure, the insulation wore through and shorted, telemetry and power were lost and the second stage was not ignited.

failures.name: Electron flight
failures.cause: Third-party ground telemetry equipment was misconfigured, so range safety lost data and terminated a healthy rocket.

failures.name: Zhongxing-9A
failures.cause: A third stage roll control thruster failed during the coast between burns, so the second burn was made in the wrong attitude.

failures.name: SJ-18
failures.cause: A structural anomaly in the turbine exhaust duct of one first stage YF-77 engine caused loss of thrust.

failures.name: Soyuz Rideshare 4
failures.cause: Several cubesats stored in one area of Fregat never worked or went to wrong orbits; Glavkosmos denied an anomaly and no cause was published.

failures.name: IRNSS-1H
failures.cause: The separation command was sent but the pyro devices did not make enough pressure to break the rivets, so the heat shield stayed on.

failures.name: Soyuz Rideshare 5
failures.cause: Fregat control algorithms were not adapted to the Vostochny launch azimuth, so the stage turned the wrong way before its first burn.

failures.name: SES-14/Al Yah 3
failures.cause: The inertial units were given a 90 degree azimuth instead of 70 degrees for this mission, so the rocket flew 17 degrees off course.

failures.name: Longjiang-1
failures.cause: This lunar microsatellite, launched with the Queqiao relay, lost contact on the way to the Moon and never entered lunar orbit; its twin Longjiang-2 succeeded. The cause is not known and the date is approximate.

failures.name: Soyuz MS-10
failures.cause: A separation sensor pin bent during assembly kept a strap-on from separating cleanly; it hit the core stage and the crew aborted.

failures.name: Weilai
failures.cause: A pipe in one third stage attitude control thruster broke, so the stage lost attitude during its burn.

failures.name: Simorgh flight
failures.cause: The third stage did not reach orbital speed per Iranian officials; no cause was published.

failures.name: Dousti
failures.cause: Iranian launch that failed to reach orbit; no cause was published.

failures.name: OS-M1 flight
failures.cause: A faulty rate gyroscope made the rocket attitude unstable and it went out of control.

failures.name: Beresheet
failures.cause: During descent one inertial measurement unit failed. A manual command sent to recover it set off a chain of events that shut down the main engine, and the lander crashed.

failures.name: Crew Dragon C201 static fire
failures.cause: Before a SuperDraco abort engine test, nitrogen tetroxide leaked through a check valve into the helium pressurization line. When the system was pressurized the slug of oxidizer was driven into a titanium check valve at high speed, which ignited and destroyed the capsule.

failures.name: Chang Zheng 4C flight
failures.cause: The third stage operated abnormally; no cause was published.

failures.name: FalconEye 1
failures.cause: A thermo-structural failure in the forward dome area of the Zefiro 23 second stage motor broke up the vehicle.

failures.name: Safir flight
failures.cause: The rocket exploded on the pad before launch; Iran gave no cause.

failures.name: Chandrayaan-2 Vikram lander
failures.cause: In the second braking phase the engines gave more thrust than expected, errors built up beyond what the guidance software could handle, and the lander hit the surface hard. The Pragyan rover was lost with it; the orbiter was fine.

failures.id: crewed_or_return:2019-11-04:Boeing CST-100 Starliner Pad Abort Test
failures.name: Boeing CST-100 Starliner Pad Abort Test
failures.cause: Only two of the three main parachutes opened because a pin linking the pilot parachute to one main parachute was not properly secured during assembly. The capsule still landed safely.

failures.name: Boeing Starliner Orbital Flight Test (OFT-1)
failures.cause: Starliner read its mission elapsed time from the Atlas V at the wrong moment and was off by about 11 hours, so it burned too much fuel and could not reach the ISS. Reviews also found a software error in the service module separation logic and blamed weak software testing.

failures.name: Simorgh flight
failures.cause: The rocket did not reach orbital speed per Iranian officials; no cause was published.

failures.name: XYZ-6
failures.cause: A malfunction occurred after launch; China never published the cause.

failures.name: Nusantara Dua
failures.cause: The satellite operator said one third stage engine failed to start; China only said the third stage was abnormal and gave no root cause.

failures.name: LauncherOne flight
failures.cause: A high-pressure LOX feed line to the NewtonThree engine broke, cutting oxidizer flow and thrust seconds after ignition.

failures.name: Electron 13 Rideshare
failures.cause: An electrical connection in the second stage was not properly secured; it heated, opened the circuit and the engine lost power.

failures.name: Jilin-1 GF02
failures.cause: The rocket failed after about a minute of flight (possibly at third stage ignition); no cause was published.

failures.name: Astra Rocket 3.1 flight
failures.cause: Noise in the guidance system made the vehicle oscillate until range safety ended the flight.

failures.name: Kuaizhou-1A flight
failures.cause: The rocket performed abnormally (upper stage); no cause was published.

failures.name: SEOSAT-Ingenio
failures.cause: Two cables to the AVUM thrust vector control actuators were swapped during integration, so the stage tumbled after ignition.

failures.name: Astra Rocket 3.2 flight
failures.cause: The upper stage mixture ratio ran slightly rich, LOX ran out and the engine shut down just short of orbit.

failures.name: InSight HP3 heat probe (mole)
failures.cause: The self-hammering heat probe could not dig past about 40 cm because the soil was cemented and gave much less friction than the design assumed, so the heat flow measurement was abandoned.

failures.name: Shuang Quxian 1 flight
failures.cause: A piece of foam insulation lodged against a first stage grid fin, then fell free, the fin swung over 30 degrees and the rocket broke up.

failures.name: Global-8/Global-9
failures.cause: A fault in the second stage igniter system corrupted signals in the engine computer, which shut the engine down.

failures.name: Simorgh flight
failures.cause: Unannounced Iranian launch seen as failed; no cause was published.

failures.name: Jilin-1 MF01
failures.cause: The fairing did not separate; reports say a silicone rubber fitting stuck on the separation bolt access covers.

failures.name: GISAT-1
failures.cause: A leak in a vent and relief valve kept the LH2 tank below required pressure, so the cryogenic stage did not ignite.

failures.name: STP-27AD1
failures.cause: Propellant leaking near the engines was ignited by exhaust; the overpressure cut the electrical link to one fuel pump and the engine shut down.

failures.name: Firefly Alpha flight
failures.cause: An electrical connector to engine 2 main fuel valve separated, the engine shut down at T+15 s and the rocket later tumbled.

failures.name: Lucy
failures.cause: One of the two fan-shaped solar arrays did not fully open and latch because its deployment lanyard did not reel in fully. Later motor pulls brought it to a stable state and the mission continues, so the loss is small.

failures.name: Nuri flight
failures.cause: A helium tank anchor in the third stage LOX tank came loose because buoyancy loads were underestimated; the leak cut oxidizer and the engine stopped early.

failures.name: Ekpress-AMU3/AMU7
failures.cause: The last Breeze-M burn was cut short and left the satellites low; no cause was published.

failures.name: Kuaizhou-1A flight
failures.cause: The rocket flew abnormally (likely third stage); no cause was published.

failures.name: Angara A5/Persei flight
failures.cause: The Persei upper stage engine did not perform its later burn; a commission was formed but no cause was published.

failures.name: Simorgh flight
failures.cause: Iran said the payloads did not reach orbital speed; no cause was published.

failures.name: VCLS Demo 2
failures.cause: A wiring configuration error fired the fairing separation out of sequence so it did not separate, and a software error then upset the upper stage.

failures.name: Jilin-1 MF01
failures.cause: GCAT notes a leak in the third stage RCS; the company did not publish a root cause.

failures.name: TROPICS 1
failures.cause: A partial injector blockage and boiling fuel with thin margins led to a chamber wall burn-through in the upper stage engine; the stage ran out of fuel early.

failures.name: EOS-02
failures.cause: Vibration at second stage separation briefly upset the accelerometers; the software declared them failed, went to salvage mode and gave an unstable orbit.

failures.name: CAPSTONE
failures.cause: After a trajectory correction burn a thruster valve stayed partly open, the craft tumbled and went into safe mode. It was recovered about a month later and reached its lunar orbit.

failures.name: Firefly Alpha flight
failures.cause: The payloads were left in a lower than planned orbit and reentered within days; no cause was published.

failures.name: Epsilon flight
failures.cause: Material from a propellant tank diaphragm seal blocked a pipe in the second stage gas-jet attitude system, so attitude was lost and the rocket was destroyed.

failures.name: LunIR
failures.cause: Wikipedia lists this Artemis I lunar flyby cubesat as failed; no cause is given. Date is the launch date.

failures.name: Lunar IceCube
failures.cause: Contact was established only briefly after deployment and then lost, so the cubesat never reached lunar orbit. Date is the launch date; the cause is not known.

failures.name: Near-Earth Asteroid Scout
failures.cause: This Artemis I cubesat was never heard from after deployment. The cause is not known.

failures.name: Team Miles
failures.cause: This Artemis I cubesat was not heard from after deployment. The cause is not known.

failures.name: OMOTENASHI
failures.cause: After deployment the cubesat was spinning with its solar cells facing away from the Sun and could not stabilize or charge, so the planned semi-hard lunar landing was abandoned.

failures.name: Artemis I Orion heat shield
failures.cause: The Avcoat heat shield lost char in more than 100 places during skip entry instead of wearing away evenly, and separation bolts showed melting. NASA later found that gases built up inside the Avcoat during the skip entry because the material was not permeable enough, causing cracking and pieces to break off.

failures.name: Soyuz MS-22
failures.cause: While docked at the ISS the service module radiator cooling loop lost all its coolant, which Roscosmos attributed to a micrometeoroid strike. The capsule returned empty and the crew came home on Soyuz MS-23.

failures.name: Zhuque-2 flight
failures.cause: The second stage vernier engines failed at main engine cutoff when excessive loads damaged a LOX feed line, leaving the stage short of orbital speed.

failures.name: CubeSat for Solar Particles (CuSP)
failures.cause: This Artemis I space weather cubesat lost contact a few weeks after deployment. The cause is not known and the date is approximate.

failures.name: Pleiades NEO 5/6
failures.cause: The carbon-carbon nozzle throat insert of the Zefiro 40 second stage eroded too fast because of a material defect, and pressure fell.

failures.name: Start Me Up
failures.cause: A dislodged fuel filter reduced fuel pump efficiency, the second stage engine ran hot and shut down early.

failures.name: RS1 flight
failures.cause: The compact launch mount caused exhaust recirculation that exceeded the base heat shield limits; hot gas started an aft fire that cut all power.

failures.name: Qaem-100 flight
failures.cause: Failure mode unknown; no cause was published.

failures.name: ALOS 3
failures.cause: Excess current in the second stage electrical system (power distribution and igniter path) cut power, so the second stage engine did not ignite.

failures.name: Terran 1 flight
failures.cause: The Aeon Vac main valves opened slower than expected and LOX vapor was ingested, so the engine never reached full thrust.

failures.name: HAKUTO-R Mission 1
failures.cause: Passing over a crater rim, the laser altimeter reading jumped and the software rejected it as faulty, so the lander thought it was on the ground while still about 5 km up and fell after running out of fuel. A late landing-site change meant this case was not covered in simulation. The UAE Rashid rover was lost with it.

failures.name: LunaH-Map
failures.cause: The propulsion system would not produce thrust, most likely because a valve was stuck, so the cubesat could not brake into lunar orbit. Loss date is approximate (mission ended in 2023).

failures.name: Lunar Flashlight
failures.cause: Three of the four thrusters underperformed, most likely because debris from manufacturing clogged the propellant lines, so the cubesat could not reach lunar orbit and NASA ended the mission.

failures.name: Cheonlima-1 flight
failures.cause: North Korea said the second stage engine started abnormally due to low reliability of the new engine and unstable fuel.

failures.name: Luna 25 (Luna-Glob lander)
failures.cause: The pre-descent orbit burn ran 127 s instead of 84 s because the control unit did not cut the engine off; the accelerometers in the BIUS-L unit were never switched on, which Roscosmos linked to commands of different priority placed in one data array. The lander crashed.

failures.name: Cheonlima-1 flight
failures.cause: North Korea said an error in the emergency blasting (destruct) system destroyed the rocket during third stage flight.

failures.name: Capella 12 Acadia-2
failures.cause: An electrical arc in the second stage high-voltage battery system cut power to the engine shortly after stage separation.

failures.name: Jilin-1 GF04B
failures.cause: The investigation found abnormal ablation of a motor nozzle, and the rocket tumbled and broke up.

failures.name: OSIRIS-REx sample return capsule
failures.cause: The drogue was released while still packed at about 100,000 ft and drifted away, but the main parachute opened as planned and the capsule landed safely. NASA's likely cause is inconsistent wiring labels in the design documents, so the drogue release and main deploy signals were wired out of order.

failures.name: Tantrum
failures.cause: A guidance, navigation and control software fault prevented the planned stage 2 relight and left the payload low.

failures.name: Peregrine Mission One
failures.cause: Hours after separation a helium pressure control valve stuck open, over-pressurized and ruptured an oxidizer tank, and the lost propellant made a lunar landing impossible. The lander re-entered Earth's atmosphere on 18 January.

failures.name: Ingenuity helicopter
failures.cause: On flight 72, far past its five-flight plan, the visual navigation lost track over featureless sand ripples, the helicopter landed hard and broke its rotor blades, ending flights (NASA/JPL investigation).

failures.name: SLIM
failures.cause: About 50 m above the surface one of the two main engines lost its nozzle, so the lander drifted and came to rest on its nose with the solar cells facing west. It still landed within 100 m of target and worked through limited sunlit periods.

failures.name: IM-1 Odysseus
failures.cause: The lander's laser rangefinders did not work because a safety switch was not enabled before flight, so it landed using a NASA demo lidar with too much sideways speed, broke a leg and tipped over. It operated for about a week.

failures.name: Tanki Uchaigegata Kogata
failures.cause: The first stage motor burn rate was mispredicted, thrust was lower than modelled and over-strict abort limits made the autonomous system destroy the rocket.

failures.name: BepiColombo
failures.cause: Unexpected electrical currents between the transfer module's solar arrays and its power unit cut the power available to the ion thrusters, so thrust fell below what the planned 2025 Mercury orbit insertion needed and arrival slipped by 11 months to November 2026.

failures.name: NK Kerolox LV flight
failures.cause: North Korea preliminarily blamed the newly developed LOX-kerosene first stage engine; no detailed cause was published.

failures.name: Boeing Starliner Crew Flight Test (CFT)
failures.cause: Five aft reaction control thrusters failed during approach to the ISS and several helium leaks appeared; thruster overheating was linked to restricted oxidizer flow. The crew came home on Crew Dragon, and in February 2026 NASA called it a Type A mishap, naming organizational causes while the exact thruster cause was still under study.

failures.name: Cubesats
failures.cause: One APU temperature reading exceeded a preset limit, software shut down the APU and the Vinci could not make its final burn.

failures.name: Yunyao-1
failures.cause: The fourth stage had an anomaly (possibly at separation); no cause was published.

failures.name: Starlink Group 9-3
failures.cause: A pressure sensor line cracked from fatigue (loose clamp) and leaked LOX; the engine ran fuel-rich and was damaged at relight.

failures.name: Tatara-1
failures.cause: A first stage nozzle control sensor gave wrong signals and flight settings were inappropriate, so the autonomous system destroyed the rocket.

failures.name: Lijian-1 flight
failures.cause: The third stage lost attitude soon after ignition and was terminated; no root cause was published.

failures.name: Ship 33
failures.cause: A stronger than expected harmonic response caused propellant leaks in the ship's aft attic, fires shut down engines and the ship was lost.

failures.name: Lunar Trailblazer
failures.cause: Contact was lost the day after launch. NASA's review found the sun-pointing software aimed the solar arrays 180 degrees away from the Sun, had not been properly tested, and wrong fault-management actions blocked recovery.

failures.name: Unknown
failures.cause: The rocket is believed to have exploded on the pad at or before ignition; China never confirmed it or gave a cause.

failures.name: IM-2 Athena
failures.cause: Noisy laser altimeter data, which the navigation filter could not use, and the dark, rough south polar terrain left the lander unsure of its height; it touched down in a crater, fell on its side, and the mission ended the next day.

failures.name: Odin (Brokkr-2)
failures.cause: AstroForge never established a solid link with its asteroid flyby craft after launch and declared the mission over on 6 March. A slow tumble and ground-station problems were suggested, but the cause is not confirmed.

failures.name: Ship 34
failures.cause: A hardware failure in a center sea-level Raptor caused propellant mixing and ignition, engines shut down and the ship was lost.

failures.name: Spectrum flight
failures.cause: A vent valve opened unintentionally at about T+25 s and the rocket lost attitude control at the start of its roll manoeuvre.

failures.name: LM-400 Tech Demo
failures.cause: Plume-induced flow separation at higher angle of attack overheated the first stage, which ruptured at separation and the pressure wave tore off the second stage nozzle extension.

failures.name: RISAT-1B
failures.cause: Chamber pressure in the third stage solid motor fell; the failure committee report was never released, so the root cause is unknown.

failures.name: HAKUTO-R Mission 2 Resilience
failures.cause: ispace found the laser rangefinder, a new model, delivered valid altitude readings much later than expected, so the lander did not slow enough and crashed with its Tenacious rover.

failures.id: crewed_or_return:2025-06-24:The Exploration Company Mission Possible (Nyx demonstrator)
failures.name: The Exploration Company Mission Possible (Nyx demonstrator)
failures.cause: The capsule survived entry but contact was lost around parachute deployment and it hit the Pacific Ocean, losing its payload. Reports say the parachutes did not deploy, but no final root cause was found in public sources.

failures.name: Eris Block 1 flight
failures.cause: The investigation found two independent failure modes in the oxidiser pump subsystem, from supplier parts, that cut engine thrust.

failures.name: WHJSW 07?
failures.cause: A short circuit or arc in second stage power wiring disabled control units and engine gimbal control, triggering self-destruct.

failures.name: Zoljanah flight
failures.cause: Suspected first stage failure seen in the exhaust; Iran gave no cause.

failures.name: Shenzhou-20
failures.cause: Just before the planned return, tiny cracks were found in a window of the return capsule, which CMSA blamed on a likely space debris strike. The capsule was judged unsafe for a crew, so the crew came home on Shenzhou-21 and Shenzhou-20 returned empty later.

failures.name: Jixing Gaofen 04C
failures.cause: The fourth stage engine shut down early; an unconfirmed report says an engine valve control cable burned through. The company published no cause.

failures.name: MAVEN
failures.cause: After 11 years in orbit, contact was lost after an occultation; fragments of telemetry showed it spinning at about 2.7 rpm, which drained the batteries. NASA ended the mission in June 2026; the root cause is still under review.

failures.name: QZS 5
failures.cause: Delamination made during manufacture of the payload adapter grew at fairing separation; the adapter failed, the satellite was lost and second stage lines were damaged.

failures.name: HANBIT-NANO flight
failures.cause: Exhaust leaked from the first stage combustion chamber at T+33 s and the chamber ruptured; the company plans to tighten assembly and quality processes.

failures.name: Soyuz Rideshare 16
failures.cause: Roscosmos called the launch a success; GCAT notes some rideshare payloads went to the wrong orbit. No cause was published.

failures.name: PSLV Rideshare 20
failures.cause: The third stage lost roll control and chamber pressure near the end of its burn, a repeat of PSLV-C61; no root cause was published.

failures.name: SJ-32
failures.cause: CASC reported a third stage anomaly in its first burn; no cause was published.

failures.name: Unk Sat 1-6
failures.cause: A first stage anomaly ended the maiden flight; a nozzle fault was reported by a blog but not confirmed by the company.

failures.name: Tatara-1R
failures.cause: The rocket was terminated about two minutes after liftoff; the company suggested a flight termination system issue but the cause is under investigation.

failures.name: Tianlong-3 flight
failures.cause: A first stage engine compartment anomaly at about T+33 s caused loss of attitude; the company has not published a cause.

failures.name: New Glenn 7x2 flight
failures.cause: A cryogenic leak froze a hydraulic line, so one BE-3U engine did not reach full thrust in the second upper stage burn.

failures.name: New Glenn 7x2 flight
failures.cause: A faulty oxygen valve on a BE-4 engine led to the booster exploding during a pre-launch static fire.

failures.name: Zhongxing-4B
failures.cause: The mission failed and Xinhua said the cause was under investigation; no cause was published.
